from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Visualization: The Cross-Section", [
            "A sphere is a perfectly round 3D shape.",
            "A flat plane slicing through creates a circle.",
            "This circle is the sphere's cross-section."
        ])
        
        # Setup 3D objects
        sphere = Sphere(radius=1.2, color=WHITE).set_opacity(0.3)
        plane = Square(side_length=2.5, color=GOLD, fill_opacity=0.5)

        # Place objects
        self.place_at_grid(sphere, 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(plane, 'C3')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(sphere), run_time=1.5)
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Rotate(sphere, angle=PI, axis=UP), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(plane), run_time=1.5)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GOLD)

    def construct(self):

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Key Takeaway", [
            "The sphere's projected shadow is pi r squared.",
            "Its total surface area is four times that.",
            "Projection provides a 2D constraint on 3D volume."
        ])
        
        # --- Animation Objects ---
        shadow = Circle(radius=1, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        shadow_label = MathTex(r"A_{shadow} = \pi r^2", font_size=24)
        
        sphere_area_parts = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.5, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.6) for _ in range(4)])
        sphere_area_parts.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(shadow), Write(shadow_label))
        self.place_at_grid(shadow, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(shadow_label, "B5")
        self.play(shadow.animate.set_color("#00FFFF"), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(sphere_area_parts))
        self.place_in_area(sphere_area_parts, "D2", "E5")
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        final_text = Text("Ratio 4:1", font_size=32, color=RED)
        self.place_at_grid(final_text, "F3")
        self.play(Write(final_text))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(RED)
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Geometric Relationship: Sphere Surface Area and Its Projected Shadow

sections.title: Prerequisite Visualization: The Cross-Section
sections.content: Briefly review the definition of a sphere and how a plane intersecting a sphere creates a circular cross-section. Use an animation of a flat slice moving through a ball to establish the concept of 'projected width'.
sections.example: Imagine a flashlight shining on a basketball; the shadow cast on a wall is a perfect circle.

sections.title: The Projection Principle: Orthographic Shadows
sections.content: Explain that when parallel light rays hit a sphere, the shadow cast (the projection) is a circle with the same radius as the sphere. Introduce the formula for the area of this circle: A_shadow = πr².
sections.example: Use a 3D model of a glowing orange held in front of a whiteboard; notice how regardless of which way the orange is turned, the circular shadow remains constant.

sections.title: Linking Shadow to Surface Area
sections.content: Introduce Archimedes' Hat-Box Theorem. Geometrically demonstrate that the surface area of a sphere (4πr²) is exactly four times the area of its projected shadow (πr²).
sections.example: Visualize a cylinder wrapped around the sphere; the 'lateral area' of the cylinder segment is equal to the 'surface area' of the sphere within that segment.

sections.title: Application: The Solar Power Challenge
sections.content: Apply the knowledge to a real-world scenario. Explain why calculating the shadow (cross-section) is crucial for understanding how much energy a spherical object (like a satellite) intercepts from the sun versus its total surface area.
sections.example: A futuristic space-bot with a spherical solar battery: It only 'sees' the sun through its projected circular area, even though its surface area is much larger.

sections.title: Summary & Key Takeaway
sections.content: Recap: Shadow = πr²; Surface Area = 4 × Shadow. Emphasize that the projection is a 2D constraint on a 3D volume.
sections.example: A final visual showing 4 circular shadows filling the 'unrolled' skin of a sphere, solidifying the 4:1 ratio.
